sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Turn “the progress of science is important” into one compact noun phrase in German.
items: Die Bedeutung des wissenschaftlichen Fortschritts ist unumstritten.
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Genitive phrases and nominalised adjectives compress information — useful in reports, dangerous in excess.

blocks.text: The genitive shows possession or a close relationship: die Bedeutung des Fortschritts, die Ergebnisse der Studie. In formal German, genitive chains can become long: die Bedeutung des wissenschaftlichen Fortschritts für die Gesellschaft.

Adjectives can be used as nouns: der Betroffene, die Studierenden, das Wichtigste. They take adjective endings and are written with a capital letter. Learn the plural forms, because they are common in reports and official texts.

blocks.title: Compression has a cost
blocks.text: A long noun phrase can be precise, but it hides the action. If the reader needs to know who does what, use a verb.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

items: Masculine and neuter nouns take -s or -es in the genitive: des Fortschritts, des Projekts.
Feminine and plural nouns have no genitive ending: der Studie, der Studien.
Adjective nouns follow adjective endings: ein Betroffener, die Betroffenen.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: Listen once, then read the example aloud.

items.example: Die Bedeutung des wissenschaftlichen Fortschritts ist unumstritten.
items.exampleEn: The significance of scientific progress is undisputed.

items.example: Die Studierenden haben Zugang zur Bibliothek.
items.exampleEn: The students have access to the library.

items.en: because of, on the basis of
items.example: Aufgrund der Ergebnisse wird die Maßnahme verlängert.
items.exampleEn: Because of the results, the measure is extended.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.de: Die Bedeutung des wissenschaftlichen Fortschritts ist unumstritten.
items.en: The significance of scientific progress is undisputed.

items.de: Die Ergebnisse der Studie wurden veröffentlicht.
items.en: The results of the study were published.
The people affected receive financial support.
items.note: Betroffene is an adjective used as a noun.

items.de: Aufgrund der neuen Regelung müssen wir den Plan ändern.
items.en: Because of the new regulation, we have to change the plan.
items.note: Aufgrund is a formal preposition with the genitive.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The tt is short and sharp: des FORT-shrits.

blocks.text: German official and academic texts use nominal style heavily: “die Durchführung der Maßnahme”, “die Berücksichtigung der Ergebnisse”. Learners often find it dense, but recognising the pattern makes long texts manageable.
Good writers balance noun phrases with verbs. A report that contains only nominalisations is hard to read, even for native speakers.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: Two researchers discuss a report sentence.

lines.speaker: Forscherin
lines.de: Dieser Satz ist zu lang. Können wir ihn teilen?
lines.en: This sentence is too long. Can we split it?

lines.speaker: Kollege
lines.de: Ja. Die Bedeutung des Fortschritts ist der Kern.
lines.en: Yes. The significance of progress is the core.

lines.speaker: Forscherin
lines.en: And who are the people affected?

lines.speaker: Kollege
lines.de: Die von der Reform betroffenen Personen. Das ist präziser.
lines.en: The people affected by the reform. That is more precise.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Genitive and adjective nouns
sections.lede: Genitive phrases and nominalised adjectives compress information.

blocks.text: Adjective nouns are declined like adjectives: ein Betroffener (nominative), den Betroffenen (accusative), der Betroffenen (genitive plural).

sections.tip: Decode long noun phrases from the last noun backwards: die Bedeutung [des wissenschaftlichen Fortschritts] → the significance of scientific progress.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Describe a report or article using one genitive phrase and one adjective noun.

model.de: Die Ergebnisse der Studie sind klar. Die Betroffenen erhalten Unterstützung. Aufgrund der neuen Regelung müssen wir den Plan ändern.
model.en: The results of the study are clear. The people affected receive support. Because of the new regulation, we must change the plan.

tips: Build the genitive phrase from the last noun backwards.
Capitalise adjective nouns: der Betroffene, die Studierenden.
Do not chain more than two genitives in one phrase.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Die Bedeutung des Fortschritt ist klar.
items.right: Die Bedeutung des Fortschritts ist klar.
items.why: Masculine nouns take -s in the genitive.

items.wrong: Die Ergebnisse der Studie wurden veröffentlichen.
items.right: Die Ergebnisse der Studie wurden veröffentlicht.
items.why: The passive needs the past participle veröffentlicht.
An adjective used as a noun is capitalised.
